title: Pipili appliqué
summary: Pipili appliqué comes from the village of Pipili in Odisha, India. Cotton cloth in red, yellow, white and green is cut into bold shapes, laid in layers on a deep-blue ground and edge-stitched, so cut-outs in the top layer show the colour beneath.
howToPlay: Pick a cloth colour and a cut shape from the tray.
Touch a square to stitch the piece down; its mirror partners are stitched too.
Copy the plan beside the cloth, then press Check.
rules: The design mirrors left to right and top to bottom, so each piece you stitch is also stitched on its partner squares.
A square counts only when its cut shape and its cloth colour both match the plan.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; undo and clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Pipili appliqué is made by families of craftspeople in and around Pipili, who cut and stitch parasols, canopies, wall hangings and bags for festivals and homes. Workshops and cooperatives keep the craft in use today.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original arrangements in the style of the tradition)
